data.narrative:
Canada Rocket Company is a seed-stage space and aerospace developer founded by Hugh Kolias and David Tenny, which has raised $6.2M to date. The sector comp universe includes 6 public peers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private competitors including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and ICEYE, though the private set lacks sufficient same-stage clustering for reliable peer-median analysis.

Of three valuation methods examined, only stage-progression proved applicable. Using total capital raised ($6.2M) as a base value proxy and applying a typical 2.5x multiplier from seed to the subsequent financing stage yields an implied valuation of $15.5M. Public-comp anchoring is not feasible—while the Space & Aerospace sector median trades at 25.3x revenue across five public tickers, Canada Rocket Company's revenue is not disclosed. Peer-median triangulation fails due to insufficient datapoints in the narrow private peer set within the same valuation tier.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $13M to $18M, with a midpoint of $16M. This range reflects a ±15% sensitivity band around the stage-progression result. The primary uncertainty stems from limited comparable data; a single methodology typically produces lower confidence than triangulated approaches. The assessment would benefit materially from either disclosed revenue figures (enabling public-comp anchoring) or additional seed-stage private comps in the aerospace vertical.
